title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 15. The Pastimes in Navadvipa and the Sight of Purushottama after the Journey to Vrindavana
html:
Gaura and Nityananda come to Advaita's house; Advaita washes Their feet and dances; He brings Shachi, and she feeds the Lord; on the remembrance day of Madhava Puri Advaita feasts the Lords and all the devotees; the Lords depart, leaving the devotees in a separation like that of the people of Vraja; reaching Purushottama, They see Jagannatha and tell of Vrindavana

Verse 1

ततश्च कृष्णचैतन्यनित्यानन्दौ जगद्गुरू।
श्रीलाद्वैताचार्यगेहं जग्मतुः प्रेमविह्वलौ॥१॥

tataśca kṛṣṇacaitanyanityānandau jagadgurū|
śrīlādvaitācāryagehaṁ jagmatuḥ premavihvalau||1||

tatah — then; cha — and; krishnachaitanya-nityanandau — Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda; jagat-guru — the two Teachers of the world; shrila-advaita-acharya-geham — to the house of Shrila Advaita Acharya; jagmatuh — went; prema-vihvalau — overwhelmed with love.

1Then Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda, the two Teachers of the world, overwhelmed with love, went to the house of Srila Advaita Acharya.

Verse 2

तौ दृष्ट्वा सहसोत्थायाद्वैताचार्यो महेश्वरः।
सगणः प्रेमविवशो धृत्वा तच्चरणाम्बुजम्॥२॥

tau dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāyādvaitācāryo maheśvaraḥ|
sagaṇaḥ premavivaśo dhṛtvā taccaraṇāmbujam||2||

tau — the two; drishtva — seeing; sahasa — at once; utthaya — rising; advaita-acharyah — Advaita Acharya; maha-ishvarah — the great lord; sa-ganah — with his followers; prema-vivashah — overcome by love; dhritva — taking hold of; tat-charana-ambujam — their lotus feet.

2Seeing Them, Advaita Acharya, the great lord, at once rose with His followers and, overcome by love, took hold of Their lotus feet;

Verse 3

प्रक्षाल्य विधिवद्धर्षात् पीत्वा शिरसि धारयन्।
ननर्त वासो धुन्वानो मत्तकेसरिविक्रमः॥३॥

prakṣālya vidhivaddharṣāt pītvā śirasi dhārayan|
nanarta vāso dhunvāno mattakesarivikramaḥ||3||

prakshalya — washing; vidhi-vat — as enjoined; harshat — in joy; pitva — drinking (the water); shirasi — on his head; dharayan — placing; nanarta — danced; vasah — his cloth; dhunvanah — waving; matta-kesari-vikramah — with the vigour of a maddened lion.

3joyfully He washed them as enjoined, drank the water and placed it on His head1, and danced, waving His cloth, with the vigour of a maddened lion.

Verse 4

तमालिङ्ग्य प्रहर्षेण प्रणम्य च पुनः पुनः।
तेन सम्पूजितौ प्रीतौ शाल्यन्नभोजनादिना॥४॥

tamāliṅgya praharṣeṇa praṇamya ca punaḥ punaḥ|
tena sampūjitau prītau śālyannabhojanādinā||4||

tam — him; alingya — embracing; praharshena — with great joy; pranamya — bowing; cha — and; punah punah — again and again; tena — by him; sampujitau — honoured; pritau — pleased; shali-anna-bhojana-adina — with a meal of fine rice and the rest.

4Joyfully embracing Him and bowing again and again, the Lords, whom He honoured with a meal of fine rice and the rest, were well pleased.

Verse 5

संकीर्तनसुखे मग्नौ तेन सार्धं जगद्गुरू।
नृत्यन्तौ भक्तवर्गैश्च वेष्टितौ परमेश्वरौ॥५॥

saṁkīrtanasukhe magnau tena sārdhaṁ jagadgurū|
nṛtyantau bhaktavargaiśca veṣṭitau parameśvarau||5||

sankirtana-sukhe — in the joy of sankirtana; magnau — immersed; tena — him; sardham — with; jagat-guru — the two Teachers of the world; nrityantau — dancing; bhakta-vargaih — by the hosts of devotees; cha — and; veshtitau — surrounded; parama-ishvarau — the two Supreme Lords.

5Immersed with Him in the joy of sankirtana, the two Teachers of the world, the two Supreme Lords, danced, surrounded by hosts of devotees.

Verse 6

तत आचार्यः सहसा वाह्यमासाद्य सत्वरम्।
आनाय्य श्रीनवद्वीपात् सभक्तां श्रीशचीं तु ताम्॥६॥

tata ācāryaḥ sahasā vāhyamāsādya satvaram|
ānāyya śrīnavadvīpāt sabhaktāṁ śrīśacīṁ tu tām||6||

tatah — then; acharyah — the Acharya; sahasa — suddenly; vahyam — a conveyance; asadya — procuring; satvaram — quickly; anayya — having brought; shri-navadvipat — from glorious Navadvipa; sa-bhaktam — with the devotees; shri-shachim — Sri Shachi; tu — indeed; tam — her.

6Then the Acharya suddenly procured a conveyance and quickly had Sri Shachi brought from glorious Navadvipa together with the devotees;

Verse 7

बुभुजे स तया चापि तथा वैष्णवपत्निभिः।
सह पाचितमन्नं च पायसादि चतुर्विधम्॥७॥

bubhuje sa tayā cāpi tathā vaiṣṇavapatnibhiḥ|
saha pācitamannaṁ ca pāyasādi caturvidham||7||

bubhuje — ate; sah — He; taya — by her; cha — and; api — also; tatha — likewise; vaishnava-patnibhih — the wives of the Vaishnavas; saha — together with; pachitam — cooked; annam — food; cha — and; payasa-adi — sweet rice and the rest; chatur-vidham — of four kinds.

7and the Lord ate the food of four kinds — sweet rice and the rest — cooked by her and by the wives of the Vaishnavas.

Verse 8

पुरीश्रीमाधवः कृष्णप्रेमानन्दसुखार्णवः।
तस्याप्याराधनतिथौ चैत्रस्य शुक्लपक्षके॥८॥

purīśrīmādhavaḥ kṛṣṇapremānandasukhārṇavaḥ|
tasyāpyārādhanatithau caitrasya śuklapakṣake||8||

puri-shri-madhavah — Sri Madhava Puri; krishna-prema-ananda-sukha-arnavah — an ocean of the bliss and joy of love for Krishna; tasya — his; api — indeed; aradhana-tithau — on the lunar day of worship; chaitrasya — of the month of Chaitra; shukla-pakshake — in the bright fortnight.

8Sri Madhava Puri is an ocean of the bliss and joy of love for Krishna. On his day of remembrance2, in the bright fortnight of the month of Chaitra,

Verse 9

द्वादश्यां भोजयामास द्वौ प्रभू साग्रहं मुदा।
तथा भक्तगणान् सर्वानाचार्योऽद्वैत ईश्वरः॥९॥

dvādaśyāṁ bhojayāmāsa dvau prabhū sāgrahaṁ mudā|
tathā bhaktagaṇān sarvānācāryo'dvaita īśvaraḥ||9||

dvadashyam — on the twelfth day; bhojayam asa — fed; dvau — the two; prabhu — Lords; sa-agraham — earnestly; muda — joyfully; tatha — likewise; bhakta-ganan — the devotees; sarvan — all; acharyah — the Acharya; advaitah — Advaita; ishvarah — the lord.

9on the twelfth lunar day, the lord Advaita Acharya joyfully and earnestly fed the two Lords, and all the devotees as well.

Verse 10

तस्यां तेन समं कृष्णचैतन्यवल्लभेन च।
स्वयं महाप्रसादं हि भुक्त्वानन्दमवाप्नुयात्॥१०॥

tasyāṁ tena samaṁ kṛṣṇacaitanyavallabhena ca|
svayaṁ mahāprasādaṁ hi bhuktvānandamavāpnuyāt||10||

tasyam — on that (day); tena — Him; samam — with; krishnachaitanya-vallabhena — with the beloved of Krishna Chaitanya; cha — and; svayam — himself; maha-prasadam — the mahaprasada; hi — indeed; bhuktva — having eaten; anandam — bliss; avapnuyat — attained.

10On that day, eating the mahaprasada together with the Lord and with the beloved of Krishna Chaitanya3, He Himself attained bliss.

Verse 11

श्रीमाधवपुरीप्रेमरसौ श्रीशचीनन्दनौ।
हरिसंकीर्तनानन्दौ भक्तैः सह ननर्ततुः॥११॥

śrīmādhavapurīpremarasau śrīśacīnandanau|
harisaṁkīrtanānandau bhaktaiḥ saha nanartatuḥ||11||

shri-madhavapuri-prema-rasau — tasting the rasa of Sri Madhava Puri's love; shri-shachi-nandanau — the two sons of Sri Shachi; hari-sankirtana-anandau — rejoicing in the sankirtana of Hari; bhaktaih — the devotees; saha — with; nanartatuh — danced.

11The two sons of Sri Shachi4, tasting the rasa of Sri Madhava Puri's love and rejoicing in the sankirtana of Hari, danced with the devotees.

Verse 12

एवं कृत्वा दिनांस्तत्र स्थित्वा मातृवशानुगौ।
तां प्रसाद्य मधुरया गिरा संशितविग्रहौ॥१२॥

evaṁ kṛtvā dināṁstatra sthitvā mātṛvaśānugau|
tāṁ prasādya madhurayā girā saṁśitavigrahau||12||

evam — thus; kritva — spending; dinan — days; tatra — there; sthitva — staying; matri-vasha-anugau — obedient to their mother's will; tam — her; prasadya — gladdening; madhuraya — with sweet; gira — speech; samshita-vigrahau — firm in resolve.

12Having spent some days there in this way, obedient to Their mother's will, They gladdened her with sweet words and, firm in Their resolve,

Verse 13

आचार्यादीन् भक्तगणांस्तथा श्रीवासकं प्रभुम्।
संसान्त्वय्य सुखेनापि गमनाय कृतोद्यमौ॥१३॥

ācāryādīn bhaktagaṇāṁstathā śrīvāsakaṁ prabhum|
saṁsāntvayya sukhenāpi gamanāya kṛtodyamau||13||

acharya-adin — the Acharya and the other; bhakta-ganan — devotees; tatha — as well as; shrivasakam — Srivasa; prabhum — the master; samsantvayya — consoling; sukhena — gently; api — indeed; gamanaya — for departure; krita-udyamau — made ready.

13having gently consoled the Acharya and the other devotees, and the venerable Srivasa as well, They made ready to leave.

Verse 14

तेषां विक्रीडितं केऽपि वर्णयन्ति महात्मनाम्।
यथा कृष्णे मधुपुरीगते श्रीव्रजवासिनः॥१४॥

teṣāṁ vikrīḍitaṁ ke'pi varṇayanti mahātmanām|
yathā kṛṣṇe madhupurīgate śrīvrajavāsinaḥ||14||

tesham — of those; vikriditam — the play; ke api — some; varnayanti — describe; maha-atmanam — great souls; yatha — as; krishne — when Krishna; madhupuri-gate — had gone to Madhupuri; shri-vraja-vasinah — the dwellers of Sri Vraja.

14Of the play of these great souls some say this: just as the people of Sri Vraja, when Krishna had gone to Madhupuri,

Verse 15

तिष्ठन्ति तन्मयाः सर्वे तथैते वैष्णवोत्तमाः।
चिन्तयन्तश्च तल्लीलां बभूवुस्तन्मयाः किल॥१५॥

tiṣṭhanti tanmayāḥ sarve tathaite vaiṣṇavottamāḥ|
cintayantaśca tallīlāṁ babhūvustanmayāḥ kila||15||

tishthanti — remain; tat-mayah — absorbed in Him; sarve — all; tatha — so; ete — these; vaishnava-uttamah — best of Vaishnavas; chintayantah — meditating; cha — and; tat-lilam — on His pastimes; babhuvuh — became; tat-mayah — absorbed in Him; kila — truly.

15all remain absorbed in Him, so these best of Vaishnavas, meditating on His pastimes, became truly absorbed in Him.

Verse 16

कृष्णरामौ च तावेतौ तत्र ते च महत्तमाः।
उपमेयगतिज्ञेयाः कृष्णप्राणा बभुः सदा॥१६॥

kṛṣṇarāmau ca tāvetau tatra te ca mahattamāḥ|
upameyagatijñeyāḥ kṛṣṇaprāṇā babhuḥ sadā||16||

krishna-ramau — Krishna and Rama; cha — and; tau etau — these two; tatra — there; te — those; cha — and; mahattamah — greatest souls; upameya-gati-jneyah — to be understood by way of comparison; krishna-pranah — whose life is Krishna; babhuh — shone; sada — always.

16These two are Krishna and Rama, and those great souls there are (the people of Vraja): so it is to be understood by way of comparison. And they, whose very life is Krishna, ever shone.

Verse 17

ततः स्वयं श्रीजगदीश्वरावुभौ श्रीमज्जगन्नाथदिदृक्षयान्वितौ।
प्रजग्मतुः श्रीपुरुषोत्तमं प्रभू स्वभक्तवृन्दैः परिसेवितौ ध्रुवम्॥१७॥

tataḥ svayaṁ śrījagadīśvarāvubhau śrīmajjagannāthadidṛkṣayānvitau|
prajagmatuḥ śrīpuruṣottamaṁ prabhū svabhaktavṛndaiḥ parisevitau dhruvam||17||

tatah — then; svayam — themselves; shri-jagat-ishvarau — the two Lords of the world; ubhau — both; shrimat-jagannatha-didrikshaya-anvitau — filled with the wish to see glorious Jagannatha; prajagmatuh — set out; shri-purushottamam — for Sri Purushottama; prabhu — the two Lords; sva-bhakta-vrindaih — by their devotees; parisevitau — attended; dhruvam — surely.

17Then the two Lords of the world Themselves, filled with the wish to see glorious Jagannatha, set out for Sri Purushottama, and Their devotees surely attended Them with service.

Verse 18

आगत्य क्षेत्रं भुवनैकबन्धू दृष्ट्वा जगन्नाथमुखारविन्दम्।
प्रेमाश्रुपूर्णौ कलधौतविग्रहौ बभूवतुर्गद्गदरुद्धकण्ठकौ॥१८॥

āgatya kṣetraṁ bhuvanaikabandhū dṛṣṭvā jagannāthamukhāravindam|
premāśrupūrṇau kaladhautavigrahau babhūvaturgadgadaruddhakaṇṭhakau||18||

agatya — coming; kshetram — to the Kshetra; bhuvana-eka-bandhu — the two sole friends of the world; drishtva — seeing; jagannatha-mukha-aravindam — the lotus face of Jagannatha; prema-ashru-purnau — streaming with tears of love; kaladhauta-vigrahau — with bodies like gold; babhuvatuh — became; gadgada-ruddha-kanthakau — with faltering, choked voices.

18Coming to the Kshetra and seeing the lotus face of Jagannatha, the two sole friends of the world, golden of form, streamed with tears of love, and Their voices faltered and choked.

Verse 19

श्रीकाशीमिश्रस्य गृहे गतौ पुनः श्रीरामकृष्णौ किल भक्तवेष्टितौ।
श्रीसार्वभौमादय एव सर्वे तत्रागताः क्षेत्रनिवासिनोऽपरे॥१९॥

śrīkāśīmiśrasya gṛhe gatau punaḥ śrīrāmakṛṣṇau kila bhaktaveṣṭitau|
śrīsārvabhaumādaya eva sarve tatrāgatāḥ kṣetranivāsino'pare||19||

shri-kashimishrasya — of Sri Kashi Mishra; grihe — to the house; gatau — went; punah — again; shri-rama-krishnau — Sri Rama and Krishna; kila — indeed; bhakta-veshtitau — surrounded by devotees; shri-sarvabhauma-adayah — Sri Sarvabhauma and the others; eva — indeed; sarve — all; tatra — there; agatah — came; kshetra-nivasinah — dwellers of the Kshetra; apare — others.

19Surrounded by devotees, Sri Rama and Krishna went again to the house of Sri Kashi Mishra; and there came all — Sri Sarvabhauma and the others, and the rest of the people of the Kshetra.

Verse 20

पश्यन्ति तत्पादसरोजवैभवं प्रणम्य भूमौ प्रणिपत्य ते मुदा।
बद्धाञ्जलि साश्रुविलोललोचनाः सगद्गदं कृष्णरसाब्धिमग्नाः॥२०॥

paśyanti tatpādasarojavaibhavaṁ praṇamya bhūmau praṇipatya te mudā|
baddhāñjali sāśruvilolalocanāḥ sagadgadaṁ kṛṣṇarasābdhimagnāḥ||20||

pashyanti — behold; tat-pada-saroja-vaibhavam — the splendour of their lotus feet; pranamya — bowing; bhumau — on the ground; pranipatya — prostrating; te — they; muda — joyfully; baddha-anjali — with joined palms; sa-ashru-vilola-lochanah — with restless, tear-filled eyes; sa-gadgadam — with faltering voices; krishna-rasa-abdhi-magnah — immersed in the ocean of Krishna's rasa.

20They behold the splendour of Their lotus feet; bowing and joyfully prostrating themselves, with joined palms, with restless, tear-filled eyes and faltering voices, they are immersed in the ocean of Krishna's rasa.

Verse 21

उत्थाय तौ सत्वरमेव तानपि आलिङ्ग्य प्रेम्णा हि मुदान्वितौ प्रभू।
वृन्दावनस्य मधुरं कथामृतं शुश्रावयामासतुरेव मानदौ॥२१॥

utthāya tau satvarameva tānapi āliṅgya premṇā hi mudānvitau prabhū|
vṛndāvanasya madhuraṁ kathāmṛtaṁ śuśrāvayāmāsatureva mānadau||21||

utthaya — rising; tau — the two; satvaram — quickly; eva — indeed; tan — them; api — also; alingya — embracing; premna — with love; hi — indeed; muda-anvitau — joyful; prabhu — the two Lords; vrindavanasya — of Vrindavana; madhuram — the sweet; katha-amritam — nectar of tales; shushravayam asatuh — made them hear; eva — indeed; mana-dau — who honour others.

21The two Lords, who honour others, rose at once, joyfully and lovingly embraced them too, and let them hear the sweet nectar of the tales of Vrindavana.

Thus ends the fifteenth sarga, "The Pastimes in Navadvipa and the Sight of Purushottama after the Journey to Vrindavana" (Shri-vrindavana-gamana-anantaram shri-navadvipa-vihara-shri-purushottama-darshana), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. That is, He honoured the water that had washed the Lords' feet as a sacred thing.
  2. Literally "on the lunar day of his worship" (aradhana), the festival in memory of a saint, usually on the anniversary of his passing. Madhava (Madhavendra) Puri was the spiritual master of Advaita and of Ishvara Puri.
  3. Nityananda.
  4. Gaura and Nityananda.
